Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All flowers are leaves.

All leaves are stems.

Some stems are roots.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some stems are leaves.

II. Some flowers are roots.

III. Some leaves are flowers.

options.text: Only conclusions II and III follow
Only conclusions I and III follow

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/79a649d46549648ad1cbe96f647ae9e4e19d49a30bf48115f1b16c2c083712c7.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some stems are leaves. → **Follows** (As, All flowers are leaves and All leaves are stems)

II. Some flowers are roots. → Does not follow (It is possible, but it is not definite)

III. Some leaves are flowers. → Follows (As, All flowers are leaves)

Hence, '**Only conclusions I and III follow**' is the correct answer.

questions.question: What type of unemployment will be generated by the agricultural sector in case when it employs additional labourers only for some time of the year like the harvest season?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Seasonal unemployment.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The scenario described in the question is a classic example of** seasonal unemployment.**
 
• It occurs when there is a predictable pattern of **employment and unemployment** in a particular sector or industry due to **seasonal changes or fluctuations** in demand.
 
• Agricultural sector is one of the most common industries where **seasonal unemployment occurs.**
 
• It is also known as** agricultural unemployment**, where farmers and other agricultural workers are employed only during the specific seasons like **harvesting, sowing, plowing, etc.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Disguised unemployment **is a situation where more people are employed in a job than actually required.

 
 
• It is often seen in the agricultural sector where a large number of people work on a small piece of land, leading to **low productivity and low wages.**
 
 
 
• **Cyclical unemployment** occurs due to the fluctuations in the business cycle.
 
 
• It is caused by changes in the economic conditions, such as** recession, depression, or boom.**
 
 
 
• **Structural unemployment **occurs due to the changes in the structure of the economy.
 
 
• It happens when there is a mismatch between the **skills of the workers and the requirements of the jobs. **

questions.question: Why did Mohammed Ali Jinnah, Madan Mohan Malaviya and Mazhar Ul Haq resign from the Imperial Legislative Council?

options.text: to protest against the Rowlatt Act
to protest against the Simon commission

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**to protest against the Rowlatt Act.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mohammed Ali Jinnah, Madan Mohan Malaviya and Mazhar Ul Haq **resigned from the** Imperial Legislative Council **to protest against the **Rowlatt Act**, which was introduced in **1919** by the British government in India.
 
• The Rowlatt Act gave the British government enormous powers to** suppress political dissent **and **curtail civil liberties**.
 
• It allowed the government to arrest and imprison anyone without **trial for up to two years.**
 
• Jinnah, Malaviya and Haq saw the Rowlatt Act as a threat to the **rights and freedoms of Indian citizens **and believed that it violated the principles of justice and democracy.
 
• By resigning from the** Imperial Legislative Council**, they wanted to show their opposition to the **Act and raise awareness **about its negative impact on Indian society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** Simon commission,** on the other hand, was appointed in **1927 **by the British government to review the working of the** Indian constitution** and **recommend changes.**
 
• **Jinnah and Malaviya **were both members of the commission, but they** resigned** from it later due to their differences with the government over the issue of Indian independence.

questions.question: Foods with starch in them will turn blue-black when they come in contact with ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**iodine.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Iodine **is a** chemical element **that is used as an indicator to test for the** presence of starch** in food.
 
• When iodine comes in contact with starch, it forms a** blue-black complex **that is visible to the naked eye.
 
• This reaction is due to the formation of an **amylose-iodine complex,** which is a type of chemical bond between iodine and starch.
 
• Salt, blue litmus, and red litmus are** not** indicators of starch and do not react with it in any way.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Iodine **is a **halogen element t**hat is commonly used as an **antiseptic, disinfectant, and nutritional supplement.**
 
• It is also used in the production of **dyes, photographic film, **and other industrial applications.
 
• **Blue litmus** is an indicator that is used to test for the** presence of acids** in a solution.

questions.question: Find the square of the sum of the digits of the smallest number divisible by both 18 and 24.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Smallest number divisible by 18 and 24 = LCM(18, 24) = 72.

Sum of digits of 72 = 7 + 2 = 9.

Square of the sum = 9² = 81.

**∴ The correct answer is 81.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The numbers are 18 and 24.

**Concept Used:**

The smallest number perfectly divisible by a given set of numbers is their Least Common Multiple (LCM).

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factorization of 18 = 2 × 3²

⇒ Prime factorization of 24 = 2³ × 3

⇒ LCM(18, 24) = Highest power of each prime factor = 2³ × 3²

⇒ LCM = 8 × 9 = 72

⇒ Smallest number divisible by both 18 and 24 is 72.

⇒ Sum of the digits of 72 = 7 + 2 = 9

⇒ Square of the sum of the digits = 9² = 81

**∴ The correct answer is 81.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

The LCM of two or more numbers is the smallest positive integer that is perfectly divisible by each of the given numbers.

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

The HCF of two or more numbers is the largest positive integer that divides each of the numbers without leaving a remainder.

questions.question: A man can row upstream at 12 km/h and downstream at 20 km/h. Find the man’s rowing speed in still water, and the rate of current.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed while rowing upstream = 12 km/h

Speed while rowing downstream = 20 km/h

**Concept:**

We need to find the rowing speed in still water and the rate of the current.

**Solution:**

Let the rowing speed in still water be R, and the rate of the current be C.

Speed while rowing upstream = R - C = 12 km/h

Speed while rowing downstream = R + C = 20 km/h

We can solve these two equations to find the values of R and C.

Adding the two equations:

⇒ (R - C) + (R + C) = 12 + 20

⇒ 2R = 32

⇒ R = 16 km/h

Substituting the value of R into one of the equations:

⇒ 16 + C = 20

⇒ C = 4 km/h

**Therefore, the rowing speed in still water is 16 km/h and the rate of the current is 4 km/h.**
